title: Quantification of Nitrogen Content in Arabica Coffee Leaves Using SPAD-502
author: Wicharuck, Suang, et al.

steps.title: Select trees and define levels
steps.instruction: Randomly choose five coffee trees (≈20 years old). For each tree, define three canopy levels: upper (average height 0.8 m), middle (0.7 m), and lower (1 m). Within each level, divide the crown into four positions as shown in Fig. 1.

steps.title: Sample leaves and record SPAD
steps.instruction: At each of the four positions per level, randomly pick three fully expanded leaves located between the 3rd and 6th leaf from the tip. Using a SPAD‑502 chlorophyll meter (Konica Minolta), take SPAD readings at four points on each leaf. This yields 5 trees × 4 positions × 3 leaves × 4 points = 240 SPAD points per level; later average the values for each position.

substeps.instruction: Identify leaf positions (3rd–6th leaf) on each branch.
Place SPAD‑502 on leaf surface and record reading at four distinct points per leaf.

steps.title: Collect leaf material for N analysis
steps.instruction: Harvest the same leaves used for SPAD measurement, label them by tree, level, and position, and transport them to the Central Laboratory, Faculty of Agriculture, Chiang Mai University for total nitrogen determination by combustion.

steps.title: Oven‑dry and grind samples
steps.instruction: Place the collected leaf samples in a drying oven set to 65 °C for three days. After drying, combine the samples from each position, then finely grind them to a homogeneous powder (20 ground samples per level).

steps.title: Weigh and encapsulate for analyzer
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.10–0.15 g of the ground leaf powder, place it into N‑free tin foil capsules, and seal them for analysis.

steps.title: Run combustion nitrogen analysis
steps.instruction: Insert the sealed capsules into the LECO nitrogen analyzer (N‑Analyzer) and run the combustion method to obtain total nitrogen concentration expressed as a percentage of dry weight.

steps.title: Calculate averages and correlations
steps.instruction: Average the SPAD readings for each position, then compute Pearson correlation coefficients (R) and coefficients of determination (R²) between SPAD values and the measured total nitrogen percentages for the upper, middle, and lower canopy levels. Perform regression analysis as described.
